newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iscor shares dive on dismal results.
newsitem.headline: Iscor shares dive on dismal results.

text.p: Shares in South African iron and steel producer Iscor Ltd tumbled on Wednesday as the market reacted to poor half year results published after the close of trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
By 0735 GMT the firm's stock had fallen 29 cents, or 8.03 percent, to 332 cents.
The firm posted a half year pre-exceptional earnings per share of 6.5 cents from 17.6 cents last time.
Iscor annnounced last August that first-half earnings would be substantially lower than in the period to December 1995.
But Iscor executive chairman Hans Smith said on Tuesday: "Trading conditions have been far more difficult than anticipated and that has affected our financial performance."
The earnings were hit by a seven percent decrease in local steel sales volumes which resulted in local sales dropping to 54 percent from 58 percent in 1995.
International dollar selling prices for steel also decreased on average by 16 percent.
The announcement of the company's results had been brought forward by three weeks to inform shareholders and the market as soon as possible of the poor results.
Operating income at the company's steel division plunged 65 percent, while its mining division managed a five percent improvement in operating income.
However, the firm did say it expected a substantial improvement in earnings in the second half of its financial year.
